Jointly estimates volume and motion, reducing artifacts caused by motion [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed algorithm is an extension of ART to 'jointly minimize the difference between acquired projections and projections of a volume warped by a displacement field' (Source [S1] notes and passages). It further describes the procedure as identifying 'both a complex and large displacement field and volume texture' (Source [S1] passages). The text explains that by warping the volume with a displacement field to account for motion before projection and unwarping corrections, the method compensates for motion, which inherently reduces motion artifacts compared to static reconstruction methods.

The claim states that standard ART or SART should be used if the object is static. However, the provided evidence (Source S1) exclusively describes 'DynART' (Dynamic ART), which is an extension of ART specifically designed for 'moving and deforming objects' and 'complex and large displacement fields'. The text details algorithms for warping and unwarping volumes based on displacement fields u(x,t). It does not contain any information or instructions regarding the use of standard ART or SART for static objects; it only discusses the dynamic case.

It extends the standard Algebraic Reconstruction Technique (ART) to account for motion by warping the volume with a displacement field before projection and unwarping the correction term before updating the static reference volume [S1].

The claim states that the method extends ART by warping the volume with a displacement field before projection and unwarping the correction term before updating the static reference volume. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.1 and Algorithm 2: 'the volume is warped with the measured displacement field... The computed projection... is compared... and the residual... is normalized and back-projected... Finally the correction term is unwarped to the frame of the undeformed state... so that it matches the reference configuration and it is added to the volume.' The mathematical formulations provided in the notes and passages ($f(x+u)$ for warping and $x-u$ for unwarping) align perfectly with the claim.
